correctness.rationale: Manhattan distance shows that distinct centers share at most two open neighbors; a trace on three elements of a hypothetical shattered four-set would contradict this when compared with the all-positive center. Every singleton has both labels. A pair is shattered exactly when it has a common center and each endpoint has a private center; a support vertex itself supplies the empty trace by bipartiteness. Straight distance-two pairs have just one common center, diagonal pairs two. This gives n-4 truncated at zero on a path, removes exactly four corner incidences for diagonal pairs in a rectangle (correcting the double subtraction of its two diagonals at 2 by 2), and leaves all distance-two pairs in d>=3. For triples, opposite neighbors on the same axis cannot be labeled positive without the third point. On three distinct axes the unique all-positive center, pairwise intermediate centers, and bipartiteness supply all but singleton traces. A singleton has a witness exactly when its chosen direction extends straight, or there is an unused direction on another axis. A fourth axis always works. In d=3 the numbers of interior axes h=3,2,1,0 give, respectively, 8 times the product, the sum of pairwise products, the sum of truncated (n_i-3), and the all-sides-at-least-3 indicator, using the interior counts (n_i-2). These counts imply the stated VC thresholds, including (2,2,3) and (2,2,4) on opposite sides of the threshold.
residual_risks: The finite trace enumeration only checks the specified small boxes. The universal result is the geometric trace argument. It uses open neighborhoods, simple paths and n_i>=2; it is not a closed-neighborhood or arbitrary induced-subgraph result.

value.rationale: The coefficients answer more than the scalar VC dimension: they locate and count every support. The private-witness criterion explains why three dimensions are genuinely boundary sensitive and why a fourth axis removes the obstruction; it decides concrete finite-box questions, such as the first cubic support appearing at 2 by 2 by 4 rather than 2 by 2 by 3. This is a structural and exact result for the natural finite induced-grid family, beyond the already known degree cap and binary counts.
residual_risks: No implications for general induced subgraphs, toroidal products, closed neighborhoods, or bigger-radius balls are established.
